data.text: All seven hosted PR checks passed on 3b23100a, including Linux full verification (21m23s), macOS subprocess/HTTP checks, native PostgreSQL, detached portability, policy and verified-tree recording. User-authorized PR #120 merged at 2026-11-16T18:57:00Z as 7cc8c82ef90bb6b2babcfab9ee60dda678311064. https://github.com/bpcakes/batter/pull/120

Downstream adoption evidence at 7cc8c82ef90bb6b2babcfab9ee60dda678311064, from 986d294c24610bbbec8809a76bdf5f78d2031a49: migrated three durable Git-observation/discovery handlers from removed job_phases to PhasedJob. A positive one-second reserve stays inside the original attempt ceiling; existing process-owned Git cleanup and SQL lease/access/generation fences remain. Successful publication runs in finalization; an atomic discovery page/receipt/successor transaction remains whole there. Borrowed finalization output uses a private single-use data slot for a consuming publication API, avoiding a potentially 256 MiB clone without driving phases locally. Strict late-settlement decline fits observations with no irreversible provider effect. Four real native phase-report regressions pass for work panic plus finalizer failure, terminal work failure plus successful finalizer, publication failure, and work timeout followed by finalization. Live PostgreSQL refresh (27), worker (12), discovery (13), and application worker (10) tests passed, including cancellation cleanup, dead letters, stale-attempt fencing and restricted publication. Locked workspace tests (674) and strict all-feature Clippy passed. This is evidence for the intended API contract, not a new defect or a request to close outstanding planned work.

fields.title: Audit copy-prone workarounds and stale consumer patterns

fields.description: Audit of 7cc8c82e: runlimit/runlimit-core/src/observation.rs:410-411 and attempts.rs:262-265 discard catch_unwind results. Dropping the caught Box<dyn Any + Send> runs application payload destructors outside containment. A callback using panic_any(Payload) where Payload::drop panics makes both helpers unwind. Both helpers are used by memory and PostgreSQL backends after state changes; the observer contract says telemetry cannot change admission results. This is a copy-prone catch-and-ignore pattern, not a default panic-hook concern. Two independent external characterization tests ran on Rust 1.100.0/macOS arm64 and confirmed an outer catch_unwind receives Err from each helper. Keep the fix native to Runlimit; do not add a dependency on Batter. Assess payload disposal rather than adding one more catch that can itself discard an arbitrary payload.
fields.acceptance_criteria: Both observer helpers contain payload destruction; string and custom payload cases are tested, including post-mutation backend behavior; document disposal and runtime limits; preserve dependency direction and run required verification.
fields.title: Contain Runlimit observer panic-payload destruction

fields.description: Audit of 7cc8c82e: worker_binary.rs:73, producer_worker/worker.rs:58, runtime crate docs and Runledger README use RuntimeShutdownSignal::ctrl_c(). shutdown_signal.rs:143-146 only wraps tokio::signal::ctrl_c, whose pinned Unix source registers SignalKind::interrupt. No SIGTERM listener exists in the native examples. A deployed copy receiving SIGTERM therefore bypasses the illustrated report classification and awaited pool closure. This is source-confirmed; no new SIGTERM subprocess experiment was run. Prefer a native library-owned SIGINT/SIGTERM signal constructor and adopt it in worker entrypoints; preserve application-installed signal policy and native ownership.
fields.acceptance_criteria: Native worker examples and quick-start handle SIGINT and SIGTERM through accounted shutdown; subprocess tests prove classification and cleanup; setup errors retained; Unix-only; public API review and docs synchronized.
fields.title: Give native worker examples a Unix termination signal path

fields.description: Audit of 7cc8c82e: runledger/runledger-runtime/examples/producer_worker/worker.rs:51 prints worker ready before Supervisor::builder_from_env(...).build() at lines 53-55. README embeds it at line 296 and instructs users to wait for that text at line 359. The example may report ready before supervisor construction fails or any loop initializes. Native startup_observer already exists. Keep definition availability distinct from worker initialization; do not imply that the observer proves database health or durable processing. Source-confirmed, not newly executed against a startup-failure fixture.
fields.acceptance_criteria: Readiness message follows RuntimeStartup::Initialized while shutdown remains driven; failure never emits ready; README and executable stay synchronized; add a startup-failure and success test.
fields.title: Publish native example readiness only after worker initialization

fields.description: Audit of 7cc8c82e: JobProgressUpdate (types/lifecycle.rs:70-80), update_job_progress and update_job_progress_for_lease (queue/lifecycle/progress.rs:312-351) are deprecated since 0.11.0 but still exported through jobs and the prelude in 0.13.0. Unlike harmless aliases, the old input preserves arbitrary JobStage writes and funnels them into shared SQL. queue_running_progress.rs:323 explicitly tests setting a claimed job back to Scheduled; typed ordinary progress cannot express that. This compatibility branch preserves a known weaker lifecycle shape, and the prelude makes it easy for a new agent to adopt. Decide a staged public cut/compatibility quarantine after checking real downstream needs; do not alter historical database migrations. Inventory older 0.1.2/0.8/0.11 aliases separately and distinguish inert aliases from invariant-restoring shims.
fields.acceptance_criteria: Recorded compatibility decision and bounded retirement scope; new-consumer guidance/prelude no longer present stage-bearing progress as ordinary integration; hard-cut obligations met if removal approved; preserve supported running/ordinary progress behavior and failure tests.
fields.title: Retire or quarantine stage-bearing progress compatibility APIs

data.text: Weeding audit batter-kw25 at 7cc8c82e confirms the propagation surface: README quick start and native worker examples call builder_from_env; downstream-agent-guide.md:1449 explicitly recommends it. config.rs:303-313 folds parse errors into absence; lines 169-188 clamp settings. Existing from_env_clamps_* tests were executed (2 passed on Rust 1.100.0/macOS arm64). Include IntentPromoterConfig::from_env and from_env_with_jobs_config_defaults: they repeat the same invalid-as-absent/clamping policy. Change the examples and these tests together with fail-closed parsing, otherwise the old behavior remains the copyable pattern.

Focused live evidence: cargo test -p runledger-postgres --test queue_running_progress stage_bearing_progress_compatibility_path_preserves_arbitrary_stage_writes --locked -- --exact passed (1 test, 2.59s) on Rust 1.100.0/macOS arm64 using the native Docker fixture. This demonstrates that arbitrary-stage compatibility remains executable behavior, not merely stale rustdoc. No migration/API removal performed.

Read-only code audit of master 7cc8c82e. Ranked actionable findings: (1) observer panic-payload destruction escapes Runlimit catch-and-ignore helpers, new batter-6p9u; (2) native worker examples only handle Ctrl-C, new batter-ad1e; (3) fail-open environment parsing/defaulting promoted by native quick start, existing batter-bwc7 with expanded propagation evidence; (4) deprecated stage-bearing progress remains in prelude and mutates arbitrary stages, new batter-hixn; (5) producer-worker example announces readiness before supervisor construction, new batter-f1j7.
ADR-010 assessment: callback disposal is a library implementation gap; dual Unix signals belong to native runtime/example integration; premature ready text is a consumer mistake with an existing startup-observer facility; environment parser is a native configuration gap; stage-bearing progress requires a bounded compatibility/cutover decision before removal. No speculative API redesign performed. Repeated body/shutdown combining in facade examples noted but not classified as a confirmed defect: helpers retain both errors and driver cleanup is separately owned. Low-level APIs and durable migration compatibility are not weeds merely for existing. Several older native aliases (since 0.1.2, 0.8, 0.11) merit a bounded inventory, prioritizing behavior-changing shims over inert aliases.
Evidence: two external observer characterization tests passed and demonstrated escaping payload-destructor panics; two native config-clamping tests passed; the live arbitrary-stage compatibility test passed. SIGTERM/readiness findings are source-confirmed, not new process experiments. No source, docs, dependencies or lockfile changed; full matrix not repeated for a read-only audit. Four new follow-ups recorded, existing config task reused; implementation remains outstanding.

data.reason: Completed copy-prone-pattern audit with five prioritized findings, four new follow-ups, existing configuration task updated and executed characterization evidence.

data.text: Implementation plan: make all three native environment readers fallible, default only missing variables, reject malformed/non-Unicode/blank/out-of-range input without retaining values. Preserve existing environment minima (lease TTL 10s, retry delay 1000ms). Direct-config validation remains unchanged. Public signature cut requires before/after docs and no infallible shim. Constructor and process-boundary regression tests cover worker and promoter paths. Signal/readiness work depends on this only at the example composition root; other fixes are independently testable. Full verify.sh after integration.

Implemented all three fallible environment readers with redacted opaque errors and builder propagation; only absence selects defaults. Preserved existing environment minima. Eight focused config tests and isolated public builder tests passed. Native Breaking migrations, ADR-010 assessment and API diff cover all three return-type cuts; no infallible shim restores silent replacement. Full scripts/verify.sh is running.

Added runtime-authored unix_termination constructor and switched both native worker examples to install SIGINT/SIGTERM before startup. Real subprocess tests pass for both signals after initialization and before supervisor submission; Ctrl-C-only negative control terminates by SIGTERM without settlement. Checked Tokio 1.54.1 registration/handler-lifetime contracts. Full verification is running.

Implemented shared native observer disposal: known String and static-str payloads release, opaque payloads/resources are forgotten without invoking arbitrary Drop. Five focused regressions pass through helpers and post-mutation memory backends; old-disposal negative control fails all five. Strict core/memory Clippy passed. Documented hook/abort/blocking limits and unbounded opaque retention; full verification running.

Removed stage-bearing type and both deprecated progress methods/reexports; private mutation admits only Preserve/Running. Source-only cut, unchanged SQL/schema, no shim because it restores arbitrary stages. 22 public entries removed, no additions; migrations cover both call shapes. Four live tests, 45 doctests and strict Clippy passed; after one extra assertion its isolated retry hit Docker Created/start timeout before SQL and cleaned up. Full final-tree verification running.

Both native worker roots now use a shared example driver that owns shutdown before observing startup; announce only Initialized and await the driver after either path. No remote-health claim. Tests prove initialization observation and stopped-startup suppression; real signals prove settlement before awaited pool closure. README snippets include the shared helper and inventory check covers all five. Full verification running.

PR #121 opened. Repository-policy CI caught one missing quick-start fixture source and stale expected count; updated the fixture, all 11 native tool-control tests pass (one existing skipped). Full local scripts/verify.sh passed formatting, file budgets and all four Clippy configurations, then failed before shared_pool SQL: Docker left the owned PostgreSQL fixture Created until startup timeout. Independent postgres:18 /bin/true probe also timed out; both owned containers removed. Hosted full suite is running at 7464e8ff.

Retirement scope is limited to the invariant-restoring progress API. Separate inventory: deprecated 0.1.2 migrate/ensure_schema_compatible aliases still delegate strict cutover checks; 0.8 retry_after/retry_at set the same lower-bound timing as replacements; 0.11 catalog job wrappers validate declared-vs-handler identity before insertion (panic wrappers wrap the same checked path); WorkflowRunRecord/WorkflowStepRecord are inert type aliases. These do not restore arbitrary stage writes and remain outside this cut. No new shim or migration changes.

Final runtime doctests pass locally after all doc edits: 14 ordinary/no-run cases plus 11 compile-fail cases. Full local verification stopped at unrelated Docker fixture startup timeout after all four Clippy configurations; exact failure and independent container-start control recorded in batter-f1j7. Hosted CI is executing the full pinned-toolchain suite at 7464e8ff.

Final documentation review corrected the new constructor example to supply the builder-required registry and propagate stopped/unsettled failures, closing the pool only after a permitted classification. These were example composition omissions; existing native MissingRegistry validation and consuming settlement variants already enforce the local boundaries. All 25 runtime doctests pass again. Production code/signatures unchanged. Hosted checks rerun for the updated exact tree.
